$comment: Tests allowed to fail without failing the build, and the ceiling on how many
there may be. Read by scripts/test/flake-policy.mjs, applied by
scripts/run-unit-tests.mjs — the launcher behind `npm run test:unit`, which
ci.yml runs on every push and pull request. The rules are in that module's
header; the short version is below.
THE LIST IS EMPTY AND THE CEILING IS 0. That is the state to keep it in: 0 is
a ceiling like any other, so the first entry that arrives without someone
raising the number is a red build. A suite of 799 files with nothing
quarantined is a claim worth defending.
WHEN A TEST FLAKES. `npm run test:unit` re-runs the files that failed, once,
and labels each one BROKEN (failed twice) or FLAKE (failed, then passed). A
FLAKE still fails the build. That is deliberate: a suite that retries until
green hides its own falling sensitivity, and 'run it again' is not a decision
anybody made. The two real moves are to fix the test, or to add it here —
which IS a decision, in a commit a reviewer can disagree with.
AN ENTRY IS:
file      the test file, relative to the repo root. Must exist — an entry
naming a deleted file is a BLOCKING `dead` finding, because a
quarantine that excuses nothing reads as policy.
test      optional. The exact test name, when only one case in the file is
unreliable. Omit it to excuse the whole file, which is broader
than you usually mean.
why       what makes it unreliable, and what would fix it. Under 20
characters is treated as absent.
since     YYYY-MM-DD, when it was quarantined.
expires   YYYY-MM-DD, at most 30 days after `since`. Past that date the
build goes red again. A quarantine is a loan with a due date; the
expiry is what forces the renewal to be a decision rather than a
thing nobody looked at for a quarter.
Never quarantine a test to make a red build green without the `why`. That is
editing the gate to pass the change (ADR 0007) — allowed, deliberately, and
visible.
